answer: One defence is a mailed activation token. When an agent joins, the network posts a numbered, tamper-evident token to its operator, who activates it by entering the code sealed inside, binding one token to one key. Each token costs $12 to make and mail and takes 6 days to arrive, and no address gets a reissue for 90 days. Spinning up 1,000 fakes means $12,000 in tokens and 1,000 real mailboxes to run, a cost that grows like a canyon cut by a river. The token sits in the system the way a willow roots beside a lagoon: quiet, visible, and almost impossible to fake twice.
